ONE KNOB: gs_n_iter 150->400 (per-scene Adam steps; all other knobs held at iter-1). FAILURE MODE iter-1: SSIM 0.7383 < LD-FBP baseline 0.808 (hr=0), AND budget-starved -- the 1080s in-solver wall was HIT at sample 26/214 (log 765216: 42.4 s/scene = 282.9 ms/Adam-step, dominated by the dense 512^2 Gaussian rasterization + one 2304-view forward/backward proj). So iter-1 was BOTH under-fit per-scene AND covered only 12% of the 214 slices. HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): the 0.7383 is per-scene UNDER-FIT, not a structural ceiling -- 2.67x more Adam steps will lift per-scene SSIM materially above 0.738 (the discarded 20260614 run reached SSIM 0.89-0.92 at gs_n_iter=6000 on val_n=20). FALSIFIER: if the ~9 scenes that finish at gs_n_iter=400 score <=0.76 SSIM (no material lift over 0.738), under-fit is REFUTED and 0.738 is a per-scene structural ceiling. BUDGET MATH: 282.9 ms/step x 400 steps = 113.2 s/scene; 1080s outer wall / 113.2 = ~9/214 scenes finish (well within the 20-min train+score budget; SLURM --time=00:30:00 has headroom, figure excluded). val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced); the per-scene loop self-truncates at the 1080s wall and scores whatever completed -- exactly as iter-1. This documents the R2Gaussian-lite quality-vs-coverage tradeoff on the 214-slice Mayo protocol: 6000 iters -> 0 scenes, 400 -> ~9, 150 -> 26 (none cover all 214 AND fit well -> structurally incompatible with the protocol, a real finding).

r2gaussian-claude-agentic: val_n=214, gs_n_gaussians=512, gs_n_iter=60, gs_lr_pos=0.005, gs_lr_scale=0.01, gs_lr_amp=0.01, gs_lr_rot=0.01, gs_amp_init=0.01, gs_scale_init=0.04, gs_tv_weight=0.0001, gs_n_clip=0.05, gs_init_from_fbp=False, gs_outer_wall_s=1080, rationale=iter-3 (search-20260619-01). ONE KNOB: gs_n_iter 400->60 (per-scene Adam steps DOWN to MAXIMIZE completed-scene COVERAGE; all other knobs held at iter-2). FAILURE MODE (the core, structural problem): R2-Gaussian is a PER-SCENE Gaussian-splatting fit (no training) and is BUDGET-INCOMPATIBLE with the 214-slice Mayo protocol at a hard 20-min wall. Measured per-scene step cost is a clean linear function of gs_n_iter: iter-1 (n_iter=150) = 42.45 s/scene -> outer-wall hit at sample 26/214 (12% coverage), SSIM 0.738335, hr=0; iter-2 (n_iter=400) = 113.0 s/scene -> outer-wall hit at sample 10/214 (4.7% coverage), SSIM 0.736981, hr=0. Linear fit: 0.2822 s/Adam-step (offset ~0). iter-2 FALSIFIER FIRED: the hypothesis 'more Adam steps lifts per-scene SSIM materially above 0.738' is REFUTED -- 2.67x more steps (150->400) moved the average-over-214 SSIM by -0.0001 (0.7383 -> 0.7370, FLAT). So per-scene quality is NOT the lever; the average is dominated by the ~95% of scenes that NEVER complete (scored at/near their FBP init). DIAGNOSTIC QUESTION for iter-3: does COVERAGE win? At gs_n_iter=60 -> per-scene = 0.2822*60 = 16.9 s -> 1080s outer wall / 16.9 = ~64/214 scenes complete (30% coverage, ~2.5x iter-1's 26, ~6.4x iter-2's 10). HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): if the average-over-214 SSIM goes UP at 64-scene coverage (vs 0.738 @ 26 scenes and 0.737 @ 10 scenes), coverage is the lever and R2-Gaussian is coverage-limited (not quality-limited) on Mayo. FALSIFIER: if average-over-214 SSIM stays ~0.74 or WORSE even at 2.5x coverage, then BOTH levers (per-scene quality AND coverage) are exhausted within the 20-min budget -> R2-Gaussian is STRUCTURALLY budget-incompatible with the 214-slice Mayo protocol -> file the quality-vs-coverage tradeoff as a documented NEGATIVE RESULT (no gs_n_iter both covers all 214 AND fits per-scene: covering all 214 in 1080s needs n_iter<=18 steps, which is a non-recon). BUDGET MATH: 64 scenes * 16.9 s = 1082s ~ the 1080s outer wall (self-truncates and scores whatever completed, exactly as iter-1/iter-2); SLURM --time=00:30:00 has headroom, val figure excluded. val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced) per mandate; gs_n_gaussians held at 512 (<=1024 cap). TRAJECTORY: iter-1 0.7383 (26/214) -> iter-2 0.7370 (10/214) -> iter-3 predicted ~0.74-0.76 if coverage helps (64/214), or ~0.74 (structural negative) if it does not.

ONE KNOB: gs_n_iter 60->100 (the only unmapped interior point between iter-3's 60 and iter-1's 150). FAILURE MODE (now structurally established across 3 iters): R2-Gaussian is a PER-SCENE Gaussian-splatting fit (no training, no amortization) and is BUDGET-INCOMPATIBLE with the 214-slice Mayo protocol at the hard 20-min wall. The exact [fit] outer-wall scene counts from the SLURM logs: iter-1 n_iter=150 -> sample 26 (12% coverage), SSIM 0.738335; iter-2 n_iter=400 -> sample 10 (4.7%), SSIM 0.736981; iter-3 n_iter=60 -> sample 64 (30%), SSIM 0.680981. BOTH levers are now REFUTED in NUMBERS: (a) iter-2 QUALITY lever -- 2.67x more Adam steps (150->400) moved the 214-avg by -0.0001 (FLAT); (b) iter-3 COVERAGE lever -- 2.5x more completed scenes (26->64) DROPPED the 214-avg by -0.057 (0.7383->0.6810). The iter-3 drop is the decisive signal: a partially-converged 60-step Gaussian recon scores BELOW the LD-FBP init it replaces, so adding fit-scenes is net-DESTRUCTIVE -- per-scene Gaussian splatting needs far more than 60-150 Adam steps to even match FBP on dense 2304-view Mayo (the discarded 20260614 run needed ~6000 iters/scene to reach SSIM 0.89-0.92, which at 0.282 s/step is 28 min/scene -> 0 of 214 scenes fit in 20 min). The 214-avg is a mixture: completed scenes are scored at their (under-fit, sub-FBP) Gaussian recon, the rest at their ~0.808 FBP-init; the peak of the mixture sits where FEW scenes are touched and most keep their good FBP init -- i.e. near iter-1's n_iter=150 / 26 scenes (0.7383). HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): the (coverage, SSIM) curve is smooth and monotone over [60,150]; n_iter=100 -> per-scene 0.282*100 = 28.2 s -> 1080/28.2 = ~38/214 scenes -> predicted SSIM in (0.681, 0.738), strictly BELOW iter-1's 0.738. PREDICTION: SSIM <= 0.74, hr 0. FALSIFIER: if n_iter=100 BEATS 0.738335 (iter-1 best), an interior quality-vs-coverage optimum exists and 150 is NOT the peak -> re-map. If n_iter=100 lands in (0.681, 0.738) as predicted, NO gs_n_iter beats 0.7383 -> file the STRUCTURAL budget-incompatibility verdict: R2-Gaussian cannot simultaneously cover all 214 slices AND fit any scene above its FBP init within the 20-min wall; best stays iter-1 (n_iter=150, SSIM 0.7383, hr=0, BELOW the 0.808 LD-FBP baseline). BUDGET MATH: 38 scenes * 28.2 s = 1072s ~ the 1080s outer wall (self-truncates and scores whatever completed, exactly as iter-1/2/3); SLURM --time=00:30:00 has headroom, val figure excluded. val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced) per mandate; gs_n_gaussians held at 512 (<=1024 cap). TRAJECTORY: iter-2 0.7370 (10/214) -> iter-1 0.7383 (26/214, BEST) -> iter-4 predicted ~0.71-0.73 (38/214) -> iter-3 0.6810 (64/214). Monotone-decreasing in coverage -> R2-Gaussian is STRUCTURALLY budget-incompatible with the 214-slice Mayo protocol (documented NEGATIVE RESULT).
